status: tested on six development inputs; not adopted
evidence: Chat decisions following that review: Breakfast alone versus the detailed guests-and-eggs subject; food plus Growing; Growing plus allotment; cover every occurrence and exclude extra meanings within each occurrence. These later decisions refine the earlier saved comments.
hypothesis: The current referent-focused wording and deletion instruction may encourage preserving details about a particular occurrence. Directly making the supplied subject's level of detail the selection criterion may reduce extra meaning while preserving details when the supplied subject actually requires them. The saved results demonstrate the problem, not this proposed cause.
changes: Interpret source passages using the complete post, rather than inviting reinterpretation of the fixed subject.
Replace both who-or-what requirements with preservation of the supplied subject's whole meaning and stated level of detail.
Retain every-occurrence coverage and combining fragments across the post.
Explicitly permit parts of words, consistent with the existing output interface.
unchanged: Opening task, identifier exclusions, word-position output instructions and input layout. No examples or case-specific prohibitions added. No previous prompt edited.
risks: Excessive trimming could omit qualifications or source evidence needed for an indirectly expressed subject.
Every-occurrence coverage must survive the narrower selection criterion.
Shorter masks are not automatically better; only removal of meaning outside the fixed subject counts as improvement.
guidance_application: Remove competing referent-preservation wording, state the desired selection criterion directly, and leave the established response contract unchanged. The official guidance does not establish that this exact wording will succeed.
